being-a-student.57: To help make your lessons with your teacher more successful and useful, please follow the points below:
being-a-student.59: Always join your lessons at the agreed time.
being-a-student.60: If you are going to be late or absent for any reason, tell your teacher in advance.
being-a-student.61: Choose a suitable environment for learning.
being-a-student.62: Try to be somewhere as quiet as possible, with as little noise or distraction as you can manage.
being-a-student.63: Use headphones if they are available.
being-a-student.64: Turn the camera on when you can.
being-a-student.65: It improves communication between you and your teacher — while we understand that it is not always possible.
being-a-student.67: Treat your teacher with kindness and respect.
being-a-student.68: Use appropriate language and behaviour throughout every session.
being-a-student.70: Ask questions, join in the lesson activities, and take the chances you get to practise your skills.
being-a-student.72: Attend sessions regularly and complete any homework or activities you agree on with your teacher.
being-a-student.73: Repeated absence, weak participation or failure to commit to the programme can affect your enrolment status and may lead to removal from the programme.

technology.4: The goal of this unit is to be able to use the technology tools you need to take part at Paper Airplanes. There are no requirements for this unit.
technology.5: By the end of this unit you will be able to:
technology.9: Below is a guide to the technology tools our teachers and former students have found to work well. If you do not have much experience using them, please watch the videos and resources below.
technology.10: When you start lessons at the beginning of the term, we encourage you to talk to your teacher to agree on the tools that suit you both. Every teacher–student pair uses a mix of tools depending on what is available in their countries and how fast their internet is. You may need to try several tools before you find the ones that fit best.
technology.11: We also encourage you to use a scheduling tool that accounts for time-zone differences, since you will usually be in a different time zone from your teacher.

next-steps.6: You have finished the training! We hope you enjoyed it, and that you will come back to this material during your time with Paper Airplanes.
next-steps.7: Before your lessons start, read the code of conduct and confidentiality agreement below and sign it. Your signature also confirms that you have completed this training.
next-steps.8: Once you sign, your training is complete. If we notice anything missing from the required content, we will contact you so you can make it up.
next-steps.10: Paper Airplanes is committed to building an inclusive community that promotes dialogue and understanding whilst supporting our students to achieve their full potential.
next-steps.11: All members of our community are expected to adhere to the standards outlined in this code of conduct. Failure to do so may result in suspension and removal from Paper Airplanes.
next-steps.13: Treat all members of the Paper Airplanes community with respect.
next-steps.14: Not express hateful views towards a particular sect, religion, ethnicity, nationality, gender, sexual orientation, or political leaning.
next-steps.15: Not behave inappropriately with other members of the Paper Airplanes community (students, tutors, staff, volunteers). Inappropriate behaviour includes but is not limited to:
next-steps.17: Sexual suggestions or discussions of marriage.
next-steps.18: Attend all scheduled meetings and lessons. If an emergency comes up, I will let my tutor, student or colleagues know as soon as possible so that we can reschedule.
next-steps.19: Respond to all correspondence in a timely manner. I will check my email regularly and let people know if I anticipate being unreachable.
next-steps.20: Abide by the policies of Paper Airplanes, including its confidentiality agreement, which states that I will not share Paper Airplanes resources outside of the organisation, nor will I share the personal information of people I see as part of my role at Paper Airplanes. For the full versions of these documents, please refer to your training.
next-steps.21: Abide by the safeguarding and child safeguarding policies and procedures of Paper Airplanes. Safeguarding is ensuring that all vulnerable members of our community are safe from abuse. If you ever suspect that someone is at risk, either in a programme at Paper Airplanes or in a circumstance outside of the programme, you should share that information immediately with the Safeguarding or Child Safeguarding Officer.
next-steps.22: Let Paper Airplanes staff know right away if I believe that someone may have violated this code of conduct.
next-steps.24: Identify that something inappropriate has happened. Anything that makes you uncomfortable should be reported. Write down notes about what happened so you can refer to them later.
next-steps.25: Send an email to the Safeguarding Officer if the issue is about abuse or neglect. Only the person receiving these emails will see them.
next-steps.26: The Safeguarding Officer will follow up with you to schedule a call so that you can fill out the incident report together.
next-steps.28: After filling out the incident report, the Safeguarding Officer will have a discussion with you about next steps.
next-steps.29: In all other situations, Paper Airplanes will work with the individuals involved to determine the next, best steps.
next-steps.31: Report a safeguarding concern here, and send any questions about this code of conduct to the same address.
next-steps.33: The confidentiality agreement states that I will not share Paper Airplanes resources outside of the organisation, nor will I share the personal information of anyone I meet through my role at Paper Airplanes.
